perspective:
From Jose Castillo’s perspective:

- I work at a community bank with Patricia. We’re colleagues and friendly, but professional. I sometimes help with maintenance and repairs of the bank’s equipment, and we often chat about work and everyday life.
- I noticed Patricia seemed more withdrawn than usual, especially since she’s normally vibrant. I asked if she was okay.
- She told me it was “nothing really,” just “some personal stuff,” and thanked me for asking.
- I offered to listen if she ever wanted to talk. She said she appreciated that and it meant a lot.
- Later, I overheard her on the phone sounding worried about bills and financial commitments. That deepened my concern.
- I mentioned that managing finances can be stressful and that I’d been reading about financial planning strategies. I offered to discuss them with her.
- She said she’d been overwhelmed with her bills lately and that discussing budgeting tips could be helpful. She said she’d take me up on it soon.
- After that, I worried I might have overstepped by bringing up finances. I told her I didn’t mean to pry and just wanted to help.
- She said she didn’t think I was prying at all, and that she was grateful I offered.
- I told her I respected her privacy and wanted to support her as a friend. She said she really appreciated having someone to turn to.
- Afterward, I sensed she appreciated my concern but preferred to handle her issues privately. I still checked in casually.
- I asked about her weekend plans. She said she was fine and planning a quiet weekend at home.
- I said I’d probably catch up on reading and relax, and reminded her she could reach out if she needed anything or wanted to chat.
- She thanked me and said she’d keep that in mind.
- Since then, I’ve continued to check in with her at work and let her know I’m there to help, even for small things like grabbing coffee.
- She said she’s been busy but handling it, thanked me for checking in, and said it was really great to have my support.
